---
title: "Installation"
---

## Requirements

- Python 3.13 or later
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) is required. The `uvx` runner ships with uv and runs every captain-hook command.

## Run without installing (default)

The fastest way to use captain-hook, with no project dependency needed:

```bash
uvx capt-hook init
```

`uvx` fetches captain-hook into a throwaway environment, runs the CLI, and discards it. Every command works the same way once you prefix it with `uvx`:

```bash
uvx capt-hook test
uvx capt-hook register-hooks
```

Run from your project root and `--hooks` defaults to `.claude/hooks`. You never add captain-hook to `pyproject.toml` and never manage a venv yourself.

## Set up from inside Claude Code

To set up without the terminal, install captain-hook as a plugin and ask Claude to do it:

```
/plugin marketplace add yasyf/captain-hook
/plugin install captain-hook@captain-hook
```

Then tell Claude **"set up captain hook"**. The `bootstrapping-hooks` skill runs `capt-hook init` for you, surveys the repo, and proposes guardrails — the same end state as the command above.

## The session reviewer

`init` (and the skill) also arm the [session reviewer](../guide/session-reviewer.qmd): when a session ends, it mines your corrections into hook pull requests. It needs an authenticated `claude` and `gh`. Skip it with `uvx capt-hook init --no-review`, or turn it off later with `uvx capt-hook review disable`.

## Pin the install

For a stable, offline-friendly setup, install captain-hook once as a uv tool. You then drop the
`uvx` prefix from every command:

```bash
uv tool install capt-hook
capt-hook init
```

To pin it in a single project's lockfile instead, for example to vendor it for offline CI,
use `uv add capt-hook`.

## Verify installation

Run the inline tests on the scaffolded example hook:

```bash
uvx capt-hook test
```

If you added captain-hook as a dependency, you can also check the import directly:

```bash
uv run python -c "import captain_hook; print(captain_hook.__name__)"
```

## Project layout

`uvx capt-hook init` scaffolds `.claude/hooks/` with a `conf.py` and a starter `example.py`, plus the bundled skills and `.claude/settings.local.json`. [Project Structure & Wiring](project-structure.qmd) walks the full layout. The exact layout is optional; `uvx capt-hook --hooks <any-dir> test` works on any directory of hooks, and the default lines up with what Claude Code looks for.

## spaCy model

Hooks that use NLP signals need the `en_core_web_sm` spaCy model; captain-hook does not auto-download it. Install it once with `python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm`. See [NlpSignal hooks need the spaCy model](../guide/troubleshooting.qmd#nlpsignal-hooks-need-the-spacy-model).

## CI integration

Run inline hook tests in CI so scaffold edits cannot ship broken expectations. `uvx capt-hook test --json` emits one JSON object per test with the fields `id`, `status`, `expected`, and `reason`, and it exits non-zero on the first failure.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/hooks.yml
name: hooks

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
      - run: uvx capt-hook test
```

`setup-uv` installs uv, which provides Python 3.13+ and `uvx`, so there's no separate Python or install step. If a downstream reporter consumes the output, drop `--json` in.
